A few hours later, a senior Russian intelligence officer landed at Moscow airport on the Aeroflot flight from London
Colonel Oleg Antonyevich Gordievsky of the KGB was at the pinnacle of his career
A stocky, athletic figure, Gordievsky strode confidently through the airport crowds
Recruited a dozen years earlier by MI6, Britain’s foreign-intelligence service, the agent codenamed NOCTON had proven to be one of the most valuable spies in history
Gordievsky’s appointment as KGB rezident (the Russian term for a KGB head of station, known as a rezidentura) had prompted rejoicing among the tiny circle of MI6 officers privy to the case
Once again, the MI6 officers went over Gordievsky’s emergency escape plan, codenamed PIMLICO, and drawn up seven years earlier in the hope that it would never have to be activated
Gordievsky had been trained to spot danger
As far as he could tell, no one followed him as he entered the familiar apartment block on Leninsky Prospekt, and took the lift to the eighth floor
The first lock on the front door opened easily, and then the second
But Gordievsky never used the third lock
